<reflection>
The first experiment provided baseline kinetic data under moderate conditions. The fitting results show that most mechanisms have very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, with differences less than 1.3, indicating that the data does not strongly discriminate among them. Mechanism M20 is a clear outlier with a much higher NLL, so it can be considered implausible. The small differences mean that many mechanisms retain non-negligible support, and the aim of the first experiment—to establish a baseline—was achieved. However, to reduce uncertainty across the entire set, a new experiment is needed that probes different kinetic regimes to amplify subtle differences.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Increasing the catalyst concentration to 0.2 M while keeping substrate at 2.0 M and no initial product will stress the system to reveal nonlinear effects. At high catalyst concentration, mechanisms involving catalyst dimerization (M2, M3) should exhibit deviations from linear scaling of rate with catalyst, as dimer formation becomes significant. Deactivation pathways that depend on catalyst concentration (e.g., M9, M13, M19) may also become more pronounced, leading to faster loss of activity over time. This condition avoids extreme substrate depletion or saturation and complements the first experiment by exploring a regime where catalyst-catalyst interactions are enhanced. It is informative for many mechanisms simultaneously because it tests for higher-order dependencies on catalyst, which differentiate simple Michaelis-Menten mechanisms from those with dimerization, deactivation, or inhibition involving catalyst species.
</hypothesis>
